messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: routing-error spike detected in eu-west-1 — multiple requests from hosted tenants are being routed to dedicated pools unexpectedly. error rate +18% for inference calls, 502/504s increasing. auto-escalation -> pager sent to #incidents oncall.

maya: oncall acked. I'm looking. paging sam for SRE assist.

aj: I'm here, saw the alert. any recent policy / rollout?

maya: yes — Platform pushed a routing-policy tweak 10m ago to change fallback order for model-variant->region->tier to prefer variant compatibility. I suspected it might be risky for cross-tier fallback but it passed staged tests.

sam: copying logs now. ops-bot can you dump the last 30m of routing decisions for a sample tenant (tenant_id=cust-###) and the policy hash? send as code.

ops-bot: // routing-snapshot
policy_hash: 0x9f7b3c
fallback_order: [model_variant, region, capacity_tier]
recent_decisions: 
- 2026-03-15T12:08:24Z tenant=cust-### routed -> dedicated-pool-eu-1 (variant mismatch tolerated)
- 2026-03-15T12:08:25Z tenant=cust-abc routed -> dedicated-pool-eu-1 (same)
- 2026-03-15T12:08:30Z tenant=cust-xyz routed -> dedicated-pool-eu-2

aj: looks like fallback_order is wrong for hosted tenants — it should prefer capacity_tier isolation before region fallback. that change allowed variant-first, which caused hosted traffic to bleed into dedicated when variant not found in hosted.

leo: paging product/CS — Tilly, do we have customer reports? impact?

tilly: hi — yes CS flagged 3 enterprise accounts reporting elevated latencies and intermittent errors since ~12:07Z. one is on Dedicated contract; ops says they saw unexpected inbound requests to their pool. customers are upset but not yet escalated to legal. I'm preparing a short message to send if we confirm root cause.

maya: mitigation plan: 1) revert policy change (quick rollback) 2) temporarily disable cross-tier variant acceptance (force error instead of spillover) 3) scale hosted variant replicas if capacity allows. we need to pick order.

sam: I can revert the config to previous hash 0x8a2d1f in the control plane now. rolling policy update will take ~30s to propagate. I'll run: 
```
# rollback
curl -XPOST https://controlplane.internal/v1/configs/policy/rollback -d '{"to_hash":"0x8a2d1f"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN'
```

ops-bot: executing rollback...
ops-bot: rollback accepted, rollout_started id=rollout-551

maya: good. once rollback is live we should measure: 1) hosted->dedicated decision rate 2) 5xx rate 3) queue lengths on dedicated pools. sam, can you flip an emergency flag to block cross-tier routing for hosted origins while rollback propagates?

sam: adding temporary ACL rule to routing-adapter: 
```
# block cross-tier accept
rbacctl set-route-rule --name block-hosted-cross-tier --match origin:hosted --action deny_accept_cross_tier
```

ops-bot: applied rule block-hosted-cross-tier -> active. routing-adapter/3 restarted.

aj: seeing immediate drop in dedicated ingress from hosted tenants in the snapshot. 5xxs starting to fall.

ops-bot: rollout status: rollout-551 completed across eu-west-1 in 22s. policy hash now 0x8a2d1f.

maya: metrics check: hosted->dedicated decision rate down 94% vs peak. 5xxs down to baseline in last 2m.

tilly: sending a brief note to affected customers: "We've identified a routing policy regression that briefly allowed hosted traffic to be directed to dedicated pools. We've rolled back the policy and applied a temporary guardrail. We're monitoring — will follow up with timeline and postmortem." Want me to cc infra?

leo: yes cc infra and account teams. good short note.

sam: root cause hypothesis: a recent policy change accidentally reordered fallback precedence to prefer model_variant over capacity_tier, which made the runtime accept incompatible variants by allowing them to land on dedicated. Why this passed staging: our staging datasets didn't exercise hosted->dedicated boundary at scale.

aj: follow-ups: - postmortem owner: aj - ensure policy rollouts have canary that validates tier isolation for any fallback change - add unit test asserting fallback_order respects capacity_tier for hosted origins - add alert for unusual cross-tier ingress rates to dedicated pools

maya: I'm adding a hotfix: will create an automated canary that simulates heavy hosted traffic for 10m after policy changes. need eng-ml signoff because variant compatibility is their area.

sam: I've unblocked accounts and removed temporary ACL after metrics stable for 5m. ops-bot removed block-hosted-cross-tier.

ops-bot: block-hosted-cross-tier removed. routing-adapter/3 steady.

tilly: customers acknowledged the message and are waiting for postmortem. no new escalations.

maya: incident update summary: rolled back policy (0x9f7b3c -> 0x8a2d1f), temporary ACL enforced/removed, dedicated pools unaffected (no resource loss), customer impact: elevated latency/5xx for ~8 minutes for 3 enterprise customers; no data leakage.

aj: paging clear? anyone else to loop in?

leo: please route postmortem to #postmortems and attach timelines. QA and eng-ml to own test coverage.

maya: clearing pager in 30m if no regressions. filing RCA draft now. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> mitigated. responders: maya, sam, aj, leo, tilly. severity: Sev2. postmortem id=PM-20260315-11
